theories.name: Queue Saturation Dynamics
theories.description: Latency variance emerges primarily from queue saturation pressure interacting with retry and concurrency limits.

theories.name: Memory Fragmentation Cascade
theories.description: Latency variance is driven primarily by memory compaction stalls triggered by thread creation limits, rather than pure queue pressure.

theories.name: Alternative to Memory Fragmentation Cascade
theories.description: An alternative latent variable explains the same observed dependencies.

theories.name: Network Route Flapping
theories.description: Latency spikes independent of queue/memory are driven by underlying BGP/routing instability dropping packets before they reach the instance.
supporting_edges: unknown_phenomena -> latency spike with zero queue pressure

theories.name: Resource Contention Dynamics
theories.description: Latency variance emerges from interacting contention layers spanning queue pressure and memory compaction behavior.
